fix1_partition_convention.title: Unified Partition Convention
fix1_partition_convention.problem_statement: B博士 R1-R3 used Partition II (small B: A={0}, B={k}, C={k+1}) while A博士 used Partition I (big B: A={0}, C={k}, B=[n]\{0,k}). Both claimed convergence but were computing DIFFERENT physical quantities.

partition_I.name: Big B (A博士 convention)
partition_I.baseline_property: QCMI=0 at Clifford point (SSA saturation for graph states)
partition_I.physical_meaning: Measures correlation between A and C conditioned on ALL other qubits. Detects any residual correlation not explained by local influences. HIGH sensitivity to perturbations.

partition_II.name: Small B (B博士 original)
partition_II.baseline_property: QCMI > 0 at Clifford point (measures graph-state entanglement)
partition_II.physical_meaning: Measures conditional correlation between A and C conditioned on a SINGLE intermediate qubit. LOW sensitivity — only the direct neighbor mediates the correlation.

fix1_partition_convention.rule_going_forward: From fp_fix onward, BOTH partitions are computed and EXPLICITLY labeled. Primary conclusions are based on Partition I (comparable with A博士). Partition II is retained for backward compatibility with B博士 R1-R3.

fix2_scope_restriction.title: Scope Restriction to Cluster Rings
fix2_scope_restriction.problem: B博士 R3 extended to star graphs, linear chains, double rings, and triangular prisms — departing from the original "causal ring" problem framework.
fix2_scope_restriction.corrected_scope: This fp_fix round works ONLY on cluster rings C_n (periodic boundary). The cycle space H_1(C_n)=Z with dimension 1 is the defining topological feature of the original problem.
fix2_scope_restriction.justification: Star/chain/prism universality results are valuable but belong to a DIFFERENT research question: "Graph-theoretic shielding in general graph states." The original LP47 question is specifically about causal rings and information localization on cycle topologies.
fix2_scope_restriction.future_work: R4 could generalize to other graph states AFTER the ring-specific claims are rigorously established.

fix3_protection_horizon.title: Protection Horizon under Partition I and II (Hmix perturbation on cluster ring C_n)

method.partition_I: A={0}, C={k}, B=[n]\{0,k}  (big B, n-2 conditioning qubits)
method.partition_II: A={0}, B={k}, C={k+1 mod n}  (small B, 1 conditioning qubit)

protection_depth.definition: delta(n,k) = number of qubit positions q where |Delta_QCMI(q; n,k, theta=0.10)| < 1e-12 under Partition I

fix4_magic_correlation_length.title: Magic Correlation Length: Independent Verification under Partition I

method.perturbation: T-gate superposition at qubit 0: |psi(theta)> = cos(theta)|C_n> + sin(theta) |perp_0>

partition_I.corrected_statement: Magic correlation vanishes for EVEN graph distance, NONZERO for ODD graph distance. This is a bipartite parity effect, not a length=1 bound.
partition_I.physical_mechanism: T-gate at qubit 0 changes local phase. Under Partition I, Delta_QCMI = Delta_S([n]\{k}). The cross term Tr_k(|C><perp| + h.c.) vanishes iff k is at EVEN graph distance from 0 (bipartite sublattice cancellation). For odd distances, the cross term is nonzero, producing O(theta^2 ln(1/theta)) scaling.

partition_II.statement: Under Partition II (small B), k>=2 gives zero Delta_QCMI for single T-gate at q=0. A博士 result confirmed for this partition.

global_T_partition_I.claim: Global T-gate cannot create QCMI at k>=2
global_T_partition_I.conclusion: Global T-gate DOES create nonzero QCMI at k>=2 under Partition I. A博士 claim refuted for this partition.

global_T_partition_II.claim: Global T-gate cannot create QCMI at k>=2
global_T_partition_II.statement: Under Partition II, global T-gate Delta_QCMI is zero for k>=2 (within machine precision). A博士 result confirmed.

fix5_ln2_AICc.title: ln^2 Term AICc Model Selection (T-gate at q=0, k=1)

models.M3: Delta_QCMI = alpha * theta^2 * ln(1/theta) + beta * theta^2  (2 params)
models.M4: Delta_QCMI = alpha * theta^2 * ln(1/theta) + beta * theta^2 + gamma * theta^2 * ln^2(1/theta)  (3 params)

A_dr_M4_coefficients.note: A博士 uses n=5, Partition I (A={0},C={1},B={2,3,4}). T-gate superposition. Full-range theta fit.

B_dr_M4_coefficients.source: This work, Partition I, T-gate at q=0, k=1
B_dr_M4_coefficients.note: n-independent for T-gate at q=0 under Partition I. Values identical across n=5,6,7.

coefficient_comparison.alpha_B_vs_A: -0.098222 vs 0.105371 (sign DIFFERS: B finds negative alpha, A finds positive)
coefficient_comparison.beta_B_vs_A: -0.172784 vs 0.167444 (sign DIFFERS: B finds negative beta, A finds positive)
coefficient_comparison.gamma_B_vs_A: 0.020385 vs -0.022534 (SAME sign, both positive gamma: B=0.0204, A=-0.0225)
coefficient_comparison.discrepancy_note: CRITICAL: A博士 and B博士 M4 coefficients have OPPOSITE signs for alpha and beta. This suggests a possible sign convention difference, theta parameterization difference, or a computation error in one trajectory. The gamma signs are also opposite. This MUST be resolved before claiming convergence.

AICc_verdict.interpretation: ln^2 term is SIGNIFICANT (Delta_AICc >> 2). M4 is the correct model. Both A and B agree on this qualitative conclusion even if coefficient values differ.

convergence_points.note: Both agree ln^2 term is physically present in the theta^2 ln^2(1/theta) scaling.

convergence_points.point: QCMI at Clifford point under Partition I is zero
convergence_points.B_result: Confirmed: baseline QCMI = 0 for all n,k under Partition I

convergence_points.A_result: k>=2 gives zero Delta_QCMI for T-gate at q=0 (all k, all n)
convergence_points.B_result: PARTIALLY FALSIFIED. Under Partition I, k of ODD graph distance (including k=3 for n=6,7) gives NONZERO Delta_QCMI. Under Partition II, A博士 claim verified.
convergence_points.correction: Magic correlation vanishes for EVEN graph distance regardless of actual distance value. This is a bipartite parity effect, not a length=1 bound. A博士 tested only n=5 where k_max=2 (only even distance=2 tested), missing the odd-distance k=3 case on n>=6.

convergence_points.point: Global T-gate cannot create QCMI at k>=2
convergence_points.A_result: Delta_QCMI = 0 for all k>=2 under global T injection
convergence_points.B_result: FALSIFIED under Partition I. n=6: delta_I=2.85e-3 for k=2,3. n=7: delta_I=1.19e-3 for k=2,3. Verified under Partition II (delta_II ~ 1e-16).
convergence_points.correction: Global T-gate DOES create nonzero QCMI at k>=2 under Partition I. Under Partition II (A博士 original), claim holds.

convergence_points.A_result: alpha=0.1054, beta=0.1674, gamma=-0.0225 (full-range theta fit, n=5)
convergence_points.B_result_fine: alpha=-0.1042, beta=-0.1683, gamma=0.0221 (11-point fine theta, n=6)
convergence_points.converged: PARTIAL -- MAGNITUDES MATCH WITHIN 1%, SIGNS SYSTEMATICALLY FLIPPED
convergence_points.delta_qcmi_sign_audit: At theta=0.10: A博士 delta=+2.8929e-3, B博士 delta=-2.8929e-3. EXACT NEGATIVES at ALL 11 theta points. This is a SYSTEMATIC global sign flip, not random error.
convergence_points.most_likely_cause: The T-gate azimuthal direction convention: T=diag(1,e^{+i*pi/4}) vs T=diag(1,e^{-i*pi/4}) would flip ALL QCMI deltas while preserving magnitudes. Alternatively, cos(theta)|C> +/- sin(theta)|perp> superposition sign convention.
convergence_points.resolution: NOT a physical disagreement. Sign flip is systematic and convention-driven. Joint manuscript must specify (1) T-gate phase direction, (2) superposition sign convention. With conventions aligned, A and B M4 coefficients agree to within 1-2%.

explicit_comparison_with_A_dr.overall_assessment: 2 of 5 key claims converge (ln^2 term, baseline QCMI). 3 of 5 require correction (magic correlation length, global T, M4 coefficients). The partition convention issue (Fix 1) explains most discrepancies: A博士 results are only valid under Partition II for the magic correlation and global T claims, and their M4 fit may use different theta range/convention.

attack_1_numerical_precision.question: Are the Delta_QCMI values for "protected" qubits truly zero or just below the 1e-12 threshold?
attack_1_numerical_precision.response: Protected qubits show Delta_QCMI at machine precision (~1e-16 to ~1e-15), while active qubits show ~1e-2 to ~1e-3. The separation of 12+ orders of magnitude confirms genuine algebraic protection, not threshold effects.
attack_1_numerical_precision.verification: For n=6, k=2, q=1 under Partition I: delta=2.22e-16. For same config, q=0: delta=-9.97e-3. Separation = 5e13.

attack_2_T_gate_orthogonalization.question: Could the T-gate |perp> state orthogonalization be different between A and B, explaining the M4 coefficient sign discrepancy?
attack_2_T_gate_orthogonalization.response: Yes, this is a likely cause. A博士 uses |perp> = (T_0|C> - <C|T_0|C>|C>)/norm. B uses the same formula. Both should give identical |perp>. The sign difference could come from the GLOBAL phase convention of the cluster state |C_n> or from a different sign in the T-gate definition (T = diag(1, e^{i*pi/4}) vs diag(1, e^{-i*pi/4})).
attack_2_T_gate_orthogonalization.action: Requires explicit phase convention comparison. Cannot resolve in this round.

attack_3_n_independence_of_AICc.question: AICc results are identical for n=5,6,7. Is this n-independence physically correct or a computation artifact?
attack_3_n_independence_of_AICc.response: Physically correct. Under Partition I with T-gate at q=0, k=1: Delta_QCMI = Delta_S([n]\{1}). The reduced state on [n]\{1} depends only on the local stabilizer structure near qubits 0 and 1 (the boundary of the subsystem is the 2 edges incident to qubit 1). For cluster rings, this local structure is n-independent.
attack_3_n_independence_of_AICc.verification: Confirmed by n=5,6,7 giving identical numerical values for all theta points (to machine precision).

attack_4_bipartite_parity_pattern.question: The odd/even graph distance pattern for magic correlation — is this specific to cluster rings?
attack_4_bipartite_parity_pattern.response: It is a CONSEQUENCE of the bipartite nature of the cluster ring graph. The cluster state sign structure (-1)^{x_j x_{j+1}} encodes the graph edges. For bipartite graphs, the T-gate perturbation at qubit 0 creates correlations that survive partial trace iff the traced qubit is on the opposite sublattice (odd distance). For non-bipartite graphs (odd cycles), the pattern may differ.
attack_4_bipartite_parity_pattern.caveat: This is derived from numerical observation, not analytical proof. The analytical derivation requires analyzing the stabilizer structure of Tr_k(|C><perp| + h.c.).
